messages:
amy: hey team — customer (AcmePayroll) opened a ticket: their nightly payroll job hit 429s halfway through and then kept failing. They say it all started when they had a short spike of requests for ~2 minutes. They mentioned 'burst credits exhausted' in the UI. Can someone confirm what the immediate mitigation is?

ben: thanks amy. quick answer: we can either (1) grant temporary burst credits, (2) advise them to smooth the job (throttle/adding delays), or (3) if this is a system bug, escalate to eng-sre. do we have headers/logs from the failed requests? those tell us if it was quota, burst, or a global throttle.

amy: copied headers from one failed request:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-per-minute: 120
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-burst-credits-remaining: 0
Retry-After: 30
x-rw-request-id: rwd-52a6
```

amy: client is batching 1000 small requests all at once (internal job fan-out). They expected short bursts to be allowed.

sarah: that header shows they hit both minute quota and used burst credits. burst-credits-remaining at 0 means the smoothing window allowed temporary excess but was consumed. do we know their plan/quota?

amy: they're on the standard dev tier: 120/minute default. job did ~800 req in 90s.

leo: rough math: 800 in 90s is ~533/min rolling avg, which will drain burst credits quickly. our burst model allows short spikes up to ~3x base for ~60s, then regenerates credits at ~1 credit/sec (per org token). once credits 0, hits per-minute limiter. we should offer concrete mitigations.

ben: agreed. Proposed next steps for support reply: 1) immediate bandaid — grant temporary burst credits for 1 hour and ask them to re-run job with small jitter. 2) recommend smoothing: client-side token bucket with concurrency cap of ~8 and inter-request jitter. 3) long term: advise reserved capacity or increase quota for recurring high-throughput jobs.

amy: can support grant credits? What's the command?

ben: yes, support can grant short TTL credits. use internal CLI: 

```
# grant 300 burst credits to org AcmePayroll for 1 hour
rw-support grant-burst --org acmepayroll --credits 300 --ttl 1h
```

ben: also include the request id from their logs when you grant so we can reconcile. after grant run, they should see \`x-rw-burst-credits-remaining\` > 0 in responses.

sarah: for the customer-facing note, include a snippet they can use to replay a small chunk and inspect headers:

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

sarah: and tell them to look for `x-rw-burst-credits-remaining`, `x-rw-rate-limit-remaining`, and `Retry-After`. if `Retry-After` is present, instruct clients to respect it and implement exponential backoff.

leo: I'm worried this might be a transparency/visibility bug — some customers reported credits not regenerating quickly after a burst. I can check regen counters for acmepayroll. if regen is slower than expected maybe a bug in the smoothing service.

amy: please escalate if you see anything odd. customer wants a quick fix — offered to grant credits now if we can.

ben: granting now and leaving notes. amy, please run the CLI and paste confirmation.

amy: ran:

```
Grant successful: org=acmepayroll credits=300 ttl=3600 grant_id=g-9f8c
```

amy: told customer to wait ~30s and re-run job at 20% concurrency with jitter. also asked them to capture headers and paste them back.

billing-bot: FYI — temporary grant recorded under invoice temporary-credits-177999. Billing note added. :receipt: 

ops-bot: Reminder: support windows >100 credits require manager approval. This grant was within allowed limits.

amy: customer reran smaller test and pasted headers:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-rw-rate-limit-per-minute: 120
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 92
x-rw-burst-credits-remaining: 268
x-rw-request-id: rwd-52d1
```

amy: success. they still plan to run full job tonight but will implement smoothing. they asked whether the platform can do server-side smoothing automatically.

ben: short answer: we have smoothing policies that apply at organization token level — they trade throughput for predictability. we can enable more aggressive smoothing for this org to reduce chance of hitting hard 429s (by spreading requests across minute windows). that's a config change on the rate-limiter service. would require ops involvement (should be low risk).

leo: if they expect heavy but short spikes regularly, recommend either: (a) upgrade to Dedicated/reserved capacity or (b) set a higher per-minute quota. smoothing helps, but it increases tail latency for everyone. be explicit about the tradeoffs.

amy: customer also asked for a repro we can attach to internal ticket. suggested steps:
1) schedule job to fan out N parallel requests (we used N=100) within 30s.
2) capture headers and request-ids.
3) run before/after grant to show burst consumption/regeneration.

sarah: adding runbook links for the team: internal runbook (rate-limiter troubleshooting): https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rate-limiter-troubleshooting

sarah: if you need eng-sre, tag @eng-sre and include grant_id and sample request ids.

leo: I'll scan regen metrics for g-9f8c and the org counters over the last 2 hours. if we see credits stuck at zero for >5min after quiet, escalate.

amy: customer is happy with temporary grant + smoothing guidance. I'll keep thread updated if anything changes. :thumbsup: 

ben: tidy follow-up for support ticket: - actions taken (grant id, TTL) - recommended customer changes (throttle, jitter, concurrency limits) - follow-up items (monitor regen metrics, consider quota increase or Dedicated). paste the sample headers and replay steps in the ticket.

leo: noted. will post metric snapshot in 15m.

amy: thanks everyone. closing loop with customer now.

(15:12) amy: posting after 15m check — regen metrics look normal: credits ramped back to ~100 in ~40s, no regen bug observed. closing on our side.

(15:35) amy: customer confirmed full job finished overnight after tuning. they opted to increase per-minute quota for recurring payroll windows. end.
